verdict.rationale: Better Auth is a self-hosted framework that stores user data in a database the integrator configures (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL and more). Community users confirm that all auth data lives in their own database with no provider lock-in, so the deployer controls where data resides. However, the product offers no explicit region or residency selection; residency follows from wherever the user deploys their database. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party region/residency control or documentation, and a residency or compliance statement covering any vendor-hosted components.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: Better Auth requires a database to store user data. You can easily configure Better Auth to use SQLite, PostgreSQL, or MySQL, and more!
You get all of your auth data in your own db in 1 cli command. You are not tied to any db provider.
It just works and I own all the data.
